title: U.S. International Transactions and Investment Position, Q3 2026 (current account / balance of payments)
source: BEA: bea.gov/news/schedule, December 2026 block, row "December 18 | 8:30 AM | News | U.S. International Transactions and Investment Position, 3rd Quarter 2026", fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 75,122 bytes) and corroborated the same session on the site's /news/schedule/full view (HTTP 200, 124,325 bytes). Promoted from `estimate` by the lane that owns this event's never-assessed research, which is exactly the confirming re-read this entry's prior source string reserved for it; `BEA:` is a confirmed-tier prefix in market-events-data.ts, and unlike the joint Census/BEA FT-900 entries this is a sole-publisher BEA release, so the joint-publisher objection that keeps those `estimate` does not reach it. The 08:30 ET time is BEA's own schedule field, not an inference
notes: Tracked for a scheduling reason before an economic one, and the 2026-09-05 initial research (docs/research/events/intl-transactions-q3-2026-12-18.md) verified the rationale while narrowing it. VERIFIED: this is the first BEA release after the 12-11 cliff — BEA's December block runs 12-02, 12-08, 12-10, THIS, 12-23, 12-23, with nothing between 12-10 and 12-18. CORRECTED: it is seven days after the 12-11 cliff, not six (six days into a lapse beginning 00:00 2026-12-12). THE FINDING THAT CHANGES HOW TO READ IT: this exact slot has already been broken once — BEA's 2025 schedule PDF (published 2024-09) put the Q3-2025 edition on 2025-12-18 and it published 2026-01-14, +27 days, the only miss in 30 Q3 vintages back to 1996 — but the 43-day 2025 lapse had ended five weeks earlier, and what moved it was the input backlog (the Sept-2025 FT-900 slipped to 2025-12-11). That channel is closed here: the Jul-Sep 2026 inputs this calendar tracks all publish pre-cliff, the last on 11-04. So the canary reads exactly one question — is BEA publishing that morning — which, on BEA's all-or-nothing 2025 behaviour (zero releases across the lapse, the one scheduled release cancelled, resumption seven days after funding returned), is the only failure channel this date still shares with gdp-q3-2026-third-2026-12-23. Failure mode if it slips is delay, not deletion: 117 releases since 1996, zero deleted, and the one disruption recovered inside a single edition. Economically it stays `low`: quarterly balance-of-payments data (current account, net international investment position) largely visible already through the monthly FT-900 reports this calendar tracks, symbols: [], no macro-keyed house playbook — and, unlike those FT-900 siblings, no nowcast channel at all, the Atlanta Fed's posted GDPNow release calendar carrying no 2026-12-18 entry (postings on 12-16, 12-17 and 12-23 bracket it). It is not solo on its date: quarterly options expiration (opex-2026-12-18) and the Bank of Japan decision (boj-decision-2026-12-18) share it and both outrank it for tape attribution.
